tickers.core_headwinds: Medical loss ratio pressure from elevated Medicare Advantage utilization and DOJ antitrust overhang; near-term catalyst is the next quarterly MLR disclosure.
tickers.deep_dive: UnitedHealth's fortress rests on Optum's vertical integration: providers, PBM and data analytics create switching costs no competitor replicates, while the insurance network effect concentrates risk-bearing scale. The utilization spike is an industry-wide cost cycle, not customers leaving — plan sponsors have nowhere else to go for integrated care at scale. The market prices UNH like a structurally broken HMO while ROIC (11.5%) still clears WACC (6.8%) comfortably and leverage stays modest at 1.9x. Overreaction, not re-rating.
tickers.tranche_plan: Tranche 1: 25-30% of intended full position at current levels. Tranche 2: 30% if next earnings shows MLR stabilizing quarter-over-quarter. Tranche 3: remainder only after DOJ overhang clears or the stock reclaims long-term support with improving margins.
invalidation_criteria: MLR deteriorates for 2 consecutive quarters beyond management guidance
DOJ action results in structural remedy forcing Optum divestiture
Net Debt/EBITDA rises above 4.0x from buybacks or settlements
